findings.passage:
The bill would direct the Secretary to compare the list provided by the Director with the voter registration rolls and investigate and then direct the county election officer to remove the names of any non-citizens that appear on the voter registration rolls within five business days. The bill would require the county election officer to notify such person that they may be reinstated on the voter registration rolls by providing proof of their citizenship.  
HB 2020 passed 32-8.  I voted yes.
findings.note: Her '2025 Senate Scene Week 10' column describes HB 2020 (quarterly list of non-citizen driver's licenses checked against voter rolls) and states she voted yes.
subjects: proof of citizenship to be reinstated on rolls

findings.passage: There was broad support in the Senate for this bill; however other amendments dealing with drop boxes and voter identification and then more concerns emerged over the practical extent of an added amendment that would have required all ballots to be hand-counted.
findings.note: Her Senate Scene column on SB 365 (advance ballots due by 7 p.m. on Election Day) says amendments on drop boxes and voter identification were added on the floor; she says the bill failed 18-22 and that she voted no, objecting to unvetted floor amendments.
subjects: voter ID amendment on the Senate floor

findings.passage: I have seen countless times over the years amendments, which are “unvetted” added to a bill on the floor and then produce unintended consequences.
findings.note: Same column: her stated reason for objecting to the floor amendments added to SB 365, which included voter-ID and drop-box changes; she also writes 'The bill failed 18-22. I voted no.'
subjects: voter ID amendment on the Senate floor

findings.passage: This topic needs further discussion with Counties and how the boxes and how many are being utilized by our County Clerks in our district – I voted NO until we have more discussion with our local elected officials.
